Two members of `ReadinessCheckName` are deliberately NOT here —
spec 316: `specsRepo` is a check TypeScript makes blocking that
aide-run-spec today does not refuse on at all, and `dashboardCheckout`
has no aide-run-spec counterpart at all (it mirrors the dashboard's
own clone-provisioning code, always non-blocking). Both are named in
the exclusion list the identifier-parity test reads, with the reason
recorded there rather than a third time here.
One entry here (`defaultBranch`: "cannot be resolved") is tested on
the TypeScript side but SKIPPED, by name, on the bash side: it cannot
be triggered by git-state manipulation without also tripping the

prerequisites.failsWhen: the project directory is not a git repository
the specs root does not exist as a directory
the default branch cannot be resolved in a root the run touches
another worktree already has the default branch checked out
a configured worktree-link entry names a path that is not on disk
